title: Graduation Haircuts: Timing the Cut for the Ceremony and Photos
hero_alt: A smiling graduate in cap and gown holding a diploma
card_text: Senior pictures and the ceremony are two dates, so plan two cuts. What shows under a cap, and which service to book.
lede: Book your graduation haircut for a few days before the ceremony, not the morning of. By then the edges have lost that raw, just-cut look, and the fade still reads sharp in every photo. If senior pictures happen on a different date, give them their own cut, timed the same way.
Here's how to plan around both dates, what still shows once the cap goes on, and which service to pick.

blocks.heading: Pictures, then the ceremony.
blocks.lead: Plan each one on its own.
paragraphs: Senior pictures and graduation day rarely fall in the same week. One haircut can't carry both, because by the second date the fade has filled in and the line-up has gone soft.
So treat them as two appointments. Once the photographer gives you a date, book a cut a few days ahead of it. When the school announces the ceremony, do the same thing again.
If the two dates sit close together, one cut may cover the pair. Text me both dates and we can work out whether a single appointment stretches that far.

blocks.heading: What the camera sees.
blocks.lead: The cap covers most of the top.
paragraphs: A mortarboard sits flat on the crown, so whatever you do with the top mostly disappears in the ceremony shots. What shows is everything below it: the sides, the line-up at the forehead and temples, the neckline, and the beard if you have one.
That makes clean sides worth more than a tall top. A skin fade or a low taper reads clearly under a cap, and a crisp line-up frames the face in close-ups with family.
A hard part, a line shaved where your hair naturally parts, stays visible on the side even with the cap on. It's also a sharp detail for senior pictures, where you'll be capless.
Leave a lot of length up top and the cap can press it into a shape you didn't plan. If you love your volume, let it be the star of the photos without the cap.

blocks.heading: Pick the service.
blocks.lead: Every one starts with the same precision cut.

items.title: Essential Haircut
items.body: The haircut, a straight razor cleanup at the neck and a finished style. Enough for a grad with a clean-shaven face.

items.title: Signature Cut
items.body: Adds a beard trim or line-up, a hot towel and razor detailing. Choose it when facial hair will be in the pictures.

items.title: Luxury Grooming Experience
items.body: Consultation, cut, beard sculpt, wash, facial steam, two hot towels, waxing, a basic design and a fragrance finish. A full reset for the day you worked toward.

items.title: Younger grads
items.body: Finishing elementary or middle school? Kids book from the same menu as everyone else, so the Essential Haircut covers a kid's graduation cut.

blocks.heading: Get on the calendar early.
paragraphs: I work solo, so every appointment comes out of one chair's week. When the ceremony date is announced, book right away instead of waiting for graduation week.
Saturdays run 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM, and the shop is closed Wednesday and Sunday. For a weekend ceremony, a Thursday or Friday appointment that same week keeps the cut close without doing it on the day.
You settle up after the cut by cash, card, Zelle or Cash App. If the plan changes, cancel in Booksy as soon as you know, since a no-show or late cancellation may be charged a fee.

items.q: When should I get a haircut before graduation?
items.a: A few days before the ceremony. The cut looks fresh in photos without the bare, just-cut edges of a same-day appointment.

items.q: Do I need a separate haircut for senior pictures?
items.a: If the photo session and the ceremony are far apart, yes. Book each cut a few days before its own date.

items.q: What haircut looks good under a graduation cap?
items.a: One with clean sides and a sharp line-up, since the cap hides most of the top. A low taper or a skin fade both read well.
